keyFindings.description: loadAskNodes (:522, :530) tests `anchor->>'artifact_id' is not null` before the guarded cast, so an ask whose anchor does not cast never falls through to block_artifact_id: its refs parent becomes the issue, while a null artifact_id falls through to the block document and both search arms (search.go:95, :329) link the same ask to the block document. The function's own doc says an ask written on a document belongs to that document. Test the castable expression (`CastableUUID(...) is not null`) in both the document join and the version case, and update TestAskNodeAnswersOverAnAnchorArtifactIDThatDoesNotCast (refs/ask_anchor_artifact_test.go:69) to expect the block document.

Anchor.UnmarshalJSON (:76) decodes every anchor twice through a wrapper: measured 3.4-3.8 us, 176 B, 4 allocs per decode vs 1.7-1.9 us, 80 B, 1 alloc for the plain struct. It runs on every anchor recordedMarkRefs decodes, and A3's proof (benchstat and replay) ran at 1f4f79e7, before this method existed. Decode into (*anchorFields)(a) first and take the slow path only on a *json.UnmarshalTypeError whose Field is artifact_id; re-run task 5(a)'s benchstat at the new head.

recordedMarksQuery (:759-763) replaced base's table-to-indexed-expression data pairing with `if table == "asks"`. Keep the pairing as data (a package var of {table, artifactID}) that recordedMarkRefs and TestRecordedMarkRefsReadsThroughTheAnchorIndexes both range over.

The three api anchor test files each carry their own copy of the stored-anchor rewrite (storeUncastableAnchor, storeNumberAnchorArtifactID, the inline update in the spelling test), the ask-list map loop and the ask.opened event decode. One storeAnchorArtifactID(t, db, askID, blockDoc, rawJSON) helper and one helper per reader.
Both doc comments enumerate their callers (`Those three are its only callers`, :20, and :40-43); a new caller or rename makes them false. State each helper's own contract only.
